html:
Snorri Sturluson was an Icelandic chieftain, poet and historian who wrote down much of what we know of Norse myth. Born in 1179, he was twice lawspeaker of the Althing, Iceland's assembly.

He is credited with two great works:

  • the Prose Edda, a handbook for poets that retells the myths of Odin, Thor and the other gods and explains the old poetic language
  • Heimskringla, the sagas of the kings of Norway from legendary times to 1177

Some think he also wrote Egil's Saga. He was one of the richest and most powerful men in Iceland in the Sturlung Age, a time of feuds between great families. He stayed at the court of King Haakon IV of Norway and became his man, promising to bring Iceland under the Norwegian crown. He did not, and lost the king's favour. In 1241 men led by Gissur Thorvaldsson, his former son-in-law, acting for the king, killed him in his cellar at Reykholt.

About twenty years later Iceland submitted to Norway, ending the Icelandic Commonwealth. His books preserve much of the pagan past of Viking Age Scandinavia.
sum: Snorri Sturluson was an Icelandic chieftain, poet and historian who wrote down much of what we know of Norse myth. Born in 1179, he was twice lawspeaker of the Althing, Iceland's assembly.
